text: 我是来自上海市革治初级中学的游文婷老师。欢迎回到我的课程。今天,我们将学习如何写上字幕,并分享我们的旅行经验。很开心和有趣,对吧?请把你的学生书,工作室和笔记准备好。看看照片,他们是什么?这是一张文件的两侧。通常,一侧有照片,一侧有信息。谁写的文件?这是陆瑶写的。她在旅行期间写的。陆瑶在哪里?Kitty请。我看到了一个很漂亮的蜜蜂。陆瑶应该去成都旅行。Jerry请。她应该看到了蜜蜂,并在关寨大街上逛逛。现在,让我们翻看文件,再看看背面。读和写陆瑶写的什么。请把你的书写好,转到第92页。终于完成了第2页,Task 2。陆瑶写的答案。陆瑶写的约会和招呼。他们在左边的顶端。陆瑶写的旅行信息。记得把旅程刻在左边。陆瑶写地址的名字也都有。pianoShark pouv陆瑶写的地址然后测试了消息,陆瑶写的地址带了信息。poll珈琪The second line shows Lisa's detailed address.Then the third line is the city.After the city, you can also write state, province, 省份, or region,地区 if necessary.Let's look at the fourth line.What's it?It is quite useful as it can help the postman deliver letters more efficiently.What about the last line?Then let's move to the message part on the left.Read it and choose what is mentioned in the postcard.Let's look at the last line.Let's check.Lu Yao wrote about the place she visited.She also shared the travelling activities and her feelings about the trip.Now, let's focus on these activities.In the second sentence, she wrote,I'm working as a volunteer.In the second sentence, she wrote,I'm working as a volunteer and helping look after lovely pandas.Here, volunteer means 志愿者These are the activities she is doing.In the third sentence, she wrote,Tomorrow, I'm going to visit a tea house and enjoy a famous Sichuan opera.Here, tea house means 茶馆and opera means 歌劇In the sentence, Sichuan opera means 川劇And she also wrote,I'm going to buy local snacks for you.These are the activities she is going to do.Why did Lu Yao share these travelling activities in the postcard?And what tins did Lu Yao use to describe the activities?Please read the message part again and think about the questions.Who would like to share your ideas?Tina, please.I think these activities are enjoyable and meaningful,so she would like to share them with Lisa.Great.Jerry, what do you think?Activities like visiting a tea house and enjoying Sichuan operahelp Lu Yao better understand the local culture and traditions.That is why Lu Yao shares these experiences with Lisa.Good point.Both of you did a good job.Here is a tip for you.Write something meaningful and interesting in the postcard.Let's move on to the next question.What tins did Lu Yao use to describe the activities?Watch the sentences carefully.You may find that Lu Yao used the present continuous tinsto describe the activities she is doingand the simple future tins to describe the activities she is going to do.Now let's conclude what we have learned from Lu Yao's postcard.First of all, we should include a date, a greeting,and a signature in the message part.What about the body part?Kitty, please.For the body part of the postcard,we should write about the place, the activities we are doing,and what we are going to do.And we should also share our feelings.Good job.We should write about the place,the activities,and the feelings during the trip.It's your turn, Jerry.Since the space on the postcard is limited,we'd better choose some meaningful and interesting activities.Well done.We should choose meaningful and interesting activities to write about.Tina, do you have something to say?Lu Yao uses the present continuous tinsto tell what she is doingand the simple future tins to tell what she is going to do.We should use tins properly.Excellent, careful girl.We should use prop tins.These are the tips on how to write a postcardto share one's travelling experience.Now it's your turn to apply what you've learned.You are going to write a postcardto share one of your travelling experiences.What's the first step?Think about what to write and organize your ideas.I'd like to introduce to you a helpful tool, an outline.Look at this outline.There are three parts,the place, the activities and the feelings.You may plan your writingby completing the outline below.Just write the key phrases.There is no need to write complete sentences.Thank you for watching.Let's look at Joe's outline.He plans to write about his travelling experience in Hangzhou.How many activities did he list?What are they?Are they meaningful, enjoyable or interesting enough?I don't think so.Let's look at them one by one.Activities one and two are in the tea garden.They sound meaningful and enjoyableand offer a cultural experience.Activity three is a must-dowhen visiting Hangzhou for most people.Activity four focuses on trying local food.It is also one of the fun parts of the trip.Activity five, buying souvenirs,allows travellers to bring a piece of their trip home.But what about activity six?This is not as exciting as the other activities.Then let's look at the feelings part.Joe thinks it is an enjoyable trip.It sounds like a fantastic experience.Here are some expressions for you.For example,I am enjoying myself.I am so excited to see so many amazing things.What a good time I am having.Boys and girls, how about your outline?Please revise it yourself.I am enjoying myself.Now it's time for you to write the postcardbased on your outline.Here is the checklist for you.Let's start.What do you think of his postcard?Joe did a good job.He included a date, a greeting, and a signature in his postcard.He also wrote about the activities and his feelings.Picking tea leaves and drinking tea are enjoyable.Walking around the West Lake and visiting the top 10 views are interesting.Tina, what do you think of Joe's work?I think Joe should be careful with the tans he used.For example, when describing future plans, we should use the simple future tans.In the sentence, in the afternoon, I'm walking around the West Lake and visiting the top 10 views.It should be, I'm going to walk around the West Lake and visit the top 10 views.Thank you, Kitty and Tina.Both of your ideas are important to Joe.In today's lesson, we've learned how to write a postcard.It is a great way to share memories and greetings with friends and families about our travels.I truly hope you can write a postcard during your next trip.What are the homework for today?Do the exercises on page 81, workbook 6A.Revise your postcard according to the checklist.See you next time.
